messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — we've been seeing streaming responses abruptly cut off mid-token, then our client reconnects and gets the rest plus duplicates. Happened ~2026-03-12 18:35 UTC. Request IDs: req_7f3a2, req_7f3a8. 2 invoices showed doubled billing. Repro: small python snippet using streaming iterator yields duplicate final chunk.

alina (support): sorry to hear this. Can you paste the request id, full client logs (headers), and which SDK versions you used? Also was this on hosted or dedicated?

acme_ops: Hosted; region us-west-2. Using redwood-python 0.9.4. Logs attached (snip):

```
SSE RECEIVED: data: {"event":"token","id":"evt-123","data":"Hello"}
SSE RECEIVED: data: {"event":"token","id":"evt-124","data":" world"}
<socket closed by peer>
Client reconnecting with Range: last_event_id=evt-124
SSE RECEIVED: data: {"event":"token","id":"evt-124","data":" world"}
SSE RECEIVED: data: {"event":"token","id":"evt-125","data":"!"}
```

acme_ops: Note duplicate id evt-124 delivered after reconnect.

ryan (py-sdk): thanks. That pattern suggests the client is requesting resume last_event_id but the server replays the chunk even though client already applied it. Could be our dedupe logic not matching id token vs content boundaries. Can you share sample code? Also which iterator pattern: `for chunk in client.stream(...):` or `async for`?

acme_ops: sync iterator: 
```
for token in client.text_stream(model="redwood-mix", prompt=...) :
    print(token)
```

ryan (py-sdk): interesting. On the sync iterator we recently changed the reconnect backoff logic in 0.9.4 to be optimistic and resume immediately — might race with application-level consumption. I'm going to try reproduce.

matt (go-sdk): we'll test go too; older go change to event id parsing happened in 0.8.1 — might be related to multi-part event payloads where id repeats across frames.

deploy-bot: Deploy r-2026-03-12T18:20 by @infra-oncall to hosted/us-west-2 (runtime change: sse-retry-optimization)

infra-oncall: I rolled that change earlier today (see deploy). Looks like sse-retry-optimization modifies keepalive/flush semantics. I'll check server-side logs for replay decisions. @billing can you correlate request IDs with duplicate charges?

billing: We're seeing two charge lines for the same request_id window for acme_ops on 2026-03-12 18:35 (UTC). We can hold refund until root cause confirmed. Please provide the exact tokens or event ids to match line items.

ryan (py-sdk): repro script (sync) I used locally:
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
it = c.text_stream("test-model", "hello")
for t in it:
    if t == " world":
        # simulate app crash before ack
        break
# reconnect
for t in it:
    print(t)
```

ryan (py-sdk): On my run I saw last event id re-sent. Next steps: add stronger dedupe of event.id at SDK level (track seen ids per stream) and add server-side check to avoid re-sending identical id when resuming if client-supplied last_event_id equals last-delivered-id.

alina (support): Action items: 1) infra to check server replay logic and whether flush/part frames can split id across frames (infra-oncall assigned). 2) ryan/matt to prototype SDK dedupe in both py & go and ship patch (ryan/matt assigned). 3) billing to hold refund until we verify double-billing (billing assigned). 4) interim mitigation: recommend clients upgrade to pinned SDK patch when available or use explicit last_event_id handling.

infra-oncall: found server logs: when chunk flush occurred mid-frame we set last_sent_event_id="evt-124" but didn't mark committed until final ack path; resume logic looks at last_committed_event_id and replays. There is a race. Rolling back sse-retry-optimization for us-west-2 to revert behavior.

matt (go-sdk): I pushed a small change to go-sdk that keeps a ring buffer of seen event ids and ignores duplicates on resume. CL: https://git.internal/redwood/go-sdk/CL/1234

ryan (py-sdk): pushed py patch to branch fix/sse-dedupe-1769. Also added a test that simulates mid-frame flush and assert we don't yield duplicate tokens. CL: https://git.internal/redwood/py-sdk/CL/4321

alina (support): acme_ops — can you test the py branch (or wait for release)? We can also enable an interim server-side dedupe for your org.

acme_ops: Thanks — we'll try the py branch and confirm. Appreciate fast triage :thumbsup:

billing: Placed a temporary credit for the duplicated invoice items and will reverse if root cause is not billing. Keep me posted with final PRs.

infra-oncall: Rolling back change now. ETA 10m. I'll post logs when rollback completed.

deploy-bot: Rollback r-2026-03-12T18:45 by @infra-oncall completed for hosted/us-west-2

acme_ops: Confirmed on their end: duplicates stopped after rollback. We'll validate SDK patch and report back.

alina (support): Marking this as resolved for now; reopen if you see further duplicates. Thanks everyone for quick response. :heart:
